# Reassess disabled OCR when its native dependency changes

## Platform difference

A disabled OH feature can reflect one dependency revision; later replacement of the native backend can restore an implementation path.

## Implementation

Bugaoshan first throws before LiteRT initialization on OH, then removes OH configuration and later publishes a release without that OCR service. Upstream replaces LiteRT preprocessing with scu_ocr_lite and packaged-model loading; the subsequent OH merge restores the newer OCR service while retaining OH package overrides.

## Applicability

This is a dependency/history lesson for Bugaoshan's recorded revisions. The source shows restoration of an app path, not measured accuracy, performance or comprehensive OH support of the replacement package.

These observations apply to the pinned project revisions below, studied on 2026-09-30 and backfilled on 2026-10-06. Unspecified SDK/device compatibility remains unknown; this is not a fresh upstream assessment.

## Pitfalls and limitations

Removing a guard while removing platform support does not prove the guarded operation started working. Do not keep reporting the older disabled state after the newer service has been integrated.

## Verification

Test model packaging, native initialization, recognizeAsync success/error paths, memory use and representative input accuracy on the chosen device/toolchain.

Evidence tier: historical source/diff studies, with commit and path existence rechecked in local Git during this backfill. No application build, dependency resolution, signing, installation or device execution was performed. Proposed checks above are acceptance criteria, not completed tests.
